haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors never go to the document service or Postgres. They are stored in conn:{connId} in Redis and published on cursor:{docId}.
haiku-low.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms; the client sends its latest position when the window ends. The node silently drops any cursor less than 50 ms after its last accepted cursor on that connection.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor until appliedRev reaches its rev, keeping only the newest held cursor per connection. It then draws it, checking seq again.
haiku-low.q4: The client calls transformPosition. If it throws HistoryGone, the cursor is dropped and the next cursor from that user replaces it. Otherwise it is drawn.
haiku-low.q5: Two tabs make one presence entry, keyed by userId. Leave is published, and the user disappears, only when the last tab closes. Which caret is drawn is not decided.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, within 2 s. After the gateway node dies, within 40 s.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis: a conn:{connId} key with 30 s TTL per connection, plus a doc:{docId}:conns set with 60 s TTL. Heartbeats every 10 s refresh both.
haiku-low.q8: Redis TTL expiry removes the dead node's conn records, and surviving nodes with sockets on the document sweep every 10 s to remove them. They publish leave on presence:{docId}, which reaches other clients.
haiku-low.q9: The accepted cursor is published on cursor:{docId}, and nodes with sockets on the document forward it to their clients. The doc does not explicitly describe the sender's own node beyond its subscription.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes to the presence and cursor channels before reading the snapshot, so it misses no event while reading.
haiku-low.q11: The client sends its cursor once after joining, so an idle user's caret is stored in conn:{connId} and included in the join snapshot.
haiku-low.q12: A cursor whose seq is not higher than the last seq shown for that connId is dropped. A higher seq is always newer.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never go to the document service or Postgres; they are stored only in Redis (conn:{connId}) and published over pub/sub.
sonnet.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms. The client keeps the latest position and sends it when the window ends. The node silently drops any cursor arriving less than 50 ms after its last accepted one on that connection.
sonnet.q3: It holds it (keeping only the newest held cursor per connection), and draws it when appliedRev reaches its rev, checking seq again at that moment.
sonnet.q4: The client calls transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev) and draws the result, remembering its seq. If the rev is too old and it throws HistoryGone, the client drops that cursor; the user's next cursor replaces it.
sonnet.q5: One list entry (presence is keyed by userId). Leave is published only when the user's last connection/tab closes (or is swept), not when one of two tabs closes.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: within 2 s. Gateway node death: within 40 s (30 s expiry plus 10 s sweep), inside the 45 s limit.
sonnet.q7: In Redis, per connection: key conn:{connId} (userId, docId, nodeId, last cursor, TTL 30 s), plus a per-document set doc:{docId}:conns (TTL 60 s). Each heartbeat pong (every 10 s) rewrites conn:{connId} with TTL 30 s and refreshes the doc set to 60 s.
sonnet.q8: The crashed node's records expire in Redis 30 s after last refresh. Surviving nodes that have sockets on that document run a sweep every 10 s, find connIds whose records are gone, remove them from the doc set, and publish leave (if the user has no other connection) on the presence channel. Those nodes then forward leave to their clients.
sonnet.q9: The accepted cursor is stored in conn:{connId} and published on Redis channel cursor:{docId}. Nodes with sockets on the document forward it to their clients. Viewers on other nodes receive it via pub/sub; the document says nothing explicit about the sender's own node beyond that nodes with sockets on the document forward it (the diagram shows only the cross-node path).
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to presence:{docId} and cursor:{docId} first, before it writes its record and reads the doc set and connection records for the snapshot, so no event is missed during the read.
sonnet.q11: The stored cursor in conn:{connId} is included in the snapshot, and each client sends its cursor once after joining so an idle user still has a stored caret for the snapshot.
sonnet.q12: Each cursor carries a seq. The receiver drops any cursor whose seq is not higher than the last seq shown for that connId, and checks seq again when a held cursor is drawn.
